🚨 CROWDSTRIKE, MINNESOTA & THE WATER-SYSTEM CYBERATTACK

More than 30 Minnesota community water systems were reportedly targeted in a coordinated cyberattack involving operational technology—the PLCs, automated controls and supporting systems governing pumps, pressure, treatment, storage and distribution.

Before the complete forensic evidence was released publicly, investigators began pointing toward “Iranian-affiliated” hackers.

Why?

President Trump publicly rejected that attribution:

“I don’t think there was an Iranian cyberattack. I think that Minnesota ought to get its act together.”

That disagreement raises the fundamental question:

Who first attributed this operation to Iran—and what forensic evidence supported that conclusion?

Let’s take a deeper look.

THE CROWDSTRIKE–MINNESOTA CONNECTION

Minnesota’s statewide Managed Detection and Response program uses CrowdStrike.

Yes, seriously.

Through MNIT’s Whole-of-State Cybersecurity Program, CrowdStrike technology protects more than 55,000 computers and servers across over 200 Minnesota cities, counties, schools, tribal governments and other public entities.

CrowdStrike was co-founded by Dmitri Alperovitch, a Russian-born American cybersecurity executive who later became deeply involved in US national-security policy.

Alperovitch has served as:

• A special adviser to the Department of Defense
• A member of the Homeland Security Advisory Council
• A member of CISA’s Cyber Safety Review Board
• Founder of the national-security policy organization Silverado Policy Accelerator

CrowdStrike Services is led by Shawn Henry, the former executive assistant director of the FBI’s Criminal, Cyber, Response and Services Branch.

This is not simply an antivirus company.

CrowdStrike operates at the intersection of private cybersecurity, federal law enforcement, intelligence attribution, national-security policy and political power.

CROWDSTRIKE, THE DNC AND RUSSIAGATE

CrowdStrike became internationally prominent after the Democratic National Committee hired it to investigate the 2016 DNC network intrusion.

CrowdStrike attributed the operation to Russian intelligence.

Instead of independently examining the original DNC servers, federal investigators relied heavily upon CrowdStrike’s forensic findings and reports.

A document declassified in 2025 by DNI Tulsi Gabbard added another layer to this relationship.

The document contained communications associated with Leonard Benardo of George Soros’s Open Society Foundations, discussing CrowdStrike as one of the resources that could be used to obtain information or “media” concerning Trump as Hillary Clinton’s campaign moved forward with the Russia narrative.

I am sure this is all a coincidence.😂

CROWDSTRIKE, UKRAINE AND TRUMP’S IMPEACHMENT

CrowdStrike appeared again during the July 25, 2019 telephone call between President Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky—the conversation that became central to Trump’s first impeachment.

According to the official transcript, Trump said:

“I would like you to find out what happened with this whole situation with Ukraine, they say Crowdstrike… The server, they say Ukraine has it.”

Trump’s question reflected a much larger dispute:

• Who possessed the original evidence from the DNC intrusion?

• Who conducted the forensic examination?

• Why did the FBI rely so heavily upon a private contractor?

• What information concerning CrowdStrike or the DNC operation potentially existed in Ukraine?

• Who controlled the evidence used to construct the Russia-attribution narrative?

Those questions were buried beneath the impeachment spectacle.

Now we discover that Minnesota was relying upon the same company during one of the largest coordinated cyberattacks reported against American water systems—while at the same time grand juries are reportedly examining organizations and activities connected to the broader Russiagate operation. 

Is that merely a coincidence? I don't think so. 

Let's do a closer examination of who had access, who controlled the evidence and who shaped the attribution...

THE ISRAEL–UKRAINE INTELLIGENCE BRIDGE

This is where the larger geopolitical map begins to take shape.

Israel and Ukraine have increasingly convergent security interests centered on the Russia–Iran partnership.

Russia has used Iranian-designed Shahed drones extensively against Ukrainian cities and infrastructure.

Ukraine possesses:

• Recovered Iranian-designed drones
• Battlefield telemetry
• Electronic signatures
• Flight and targeting data
• Russian operational information
• Thousands of real-world encounters with Iranian technology

Israel possesses:

• Extensive intelligence concerning Iran
• Signals-intelligence capabilities
• Technical knowledge of Iranian weapons
• Intelligence on Iranian procurement networks
• Decades of operations directed against Iranian military capabilities

Ukraine requested Israeli intelligence concerning Iran’s support for the Russian military in 2022.

Zelensky later confirmed that Israel was providing intelligence about Iranian drones.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog publicly displayed evidence connecting drones recovered in Ukraine to Iranian models and described that evidence as only the “tip of the iceberg” of the available intelligence.

That creates a direct intelligence feedback loop:

Iranian technology flows to Russia.
Russia deploys it against Ukraine.

Ukraine collects battlefield evidence.

Israel contributes intelligence about the Iranian systems and networks.

Ukraine and Israel jointly expand their understanding of Iranian military capabilities.

The relationship is not hypothetical. It is documented.

THE MILITARY CONNECTION
Israel initially resisted providing Ukraine with major offensive weapons and Iron Dome because Israel needed to preserve its freedom of operation around Russian forces in Syria.

However, military and security cooperation continued developing through:

• Israeli missile-and-drone warning technology for Kyiv
• Civil-defense and emergency-management cooperation
• Intelligence concerning Iranian drones
• Ukrainian analysis of Iranian weapons
• Israeli humanitarian and battlefield medical assistance
• Discussions about transferring Russian weapons captured by Israel
• The reported movement of retired Israeli Patriot equipment through the United States for Ukrainian use

Ukraine’s battlefield experience with Iranian drones is extremely valuable to Israel.

Israel’s intelligence concerning Iran is extremely valuable to Ukraine.

Russia and Iran cooperate.

Ukraine and Israel consequently have a shared interest in countering both.

THE POLITICAL CONNECTION
The political relationship operates at several levels.

Zelensky and Netanyahu have maintained direct communications concerning:

• Civil defense
• Missile and drone threats
• Intelligence cooperation
• Ukrainian sovereignty
• Israeli security
• Iran
• Russia
• US military and political support

Recently, Benjamin Netanyahu and Zelensky were both in Washington during the same general period.

That followed Laura Loomer’s interview with Zelensky.

Who connected those circles? I wonder...

Was it merely media outreach, or are political intermediaries coordinating communications between the Ukrainian, Israeli and American political establishments?

The United States serves as the central hub connecting both governments through weapons, intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, sanctions policy and political support.

For the current event in Minnesota the relationship can be mapped like this:

MINNESOTA GOVERNMENT
↓
CROWDSTRIKE AND US CYBER CONTRACTORS
↓
FBI, DHS, CISA AND NATIONAL-SECURITY POLICY NETWORKS
↓
ISRAELI CYBERSECURITY AND UNIT 8200 ECOSYSTEM
↓
ISRAEL–UKRAINE INTELLIGENCE COOPERATION
↓
SHARED FOCUS ON RUSSIA AND IRAN
↓
ATTRIBUTION OF THE MINNESOTA ATTACK TO “IRANIAN-AFFILIATED” ACTORS

THE UKRAINIAN POLITICAL-BUSINESS LAYER
There is also a private political and oligarchic connection.

Ukrainian-Israeli oligarch Ihor Kolomoisky owned the television network that broadcast Zelensky’s programs and helped establish his national political profile.

Kolomoisky reportedly held Israeli citizenship and lived in Israel during periods of political and legal pressure in Ukraine.

Zelensky denied being controlled by Kolomoisky, and his government later moved against the oligarch.

Nevertheless, Kolomoisky represents an important bridge between:

• Ukrainian politics
• Israeli residency and citizenship networks
• Ukrainian media
• Banking and private capital
• Zelensky’s political rise
• American political intermediaries

That does not exist in isolation.

It is part of a broader transnational network where political influence, intelligence relationships, financial interests, private technology companies and national-security operations repeatedly overlap.

REPORTS OF UKRAINIAN INTELLIGENCE OPERATIONS
Reports also recently claimed that Ukrainian intelligence personnel were operating in Iraq and working with militia groups to manufacture false-flag operations against the Iraqi government.

That same Iraqi government had recently come to Washington, met with President Trump and negotiated major energy-infrastructure agreements.

If those reports are accurate, several questions follow:

• Who authorized the Ukrainian operation?

• What interests would benefit from destabilizing the Iraqi government?

• Would destabilization threaten the energy agreements reached with Trump?

• Did Israeli, Ukrainian or Western intelligence services possess advance knowledge?

• Was Iran intended to receive the blame?

• Would the resulting escalation benefit actors seeking a broader confrontation with Iran?

That alleged operation must be examined alongside the Minnesota cyberattack—not because they are automatically the same operation, but because the geopolitical incentives and attribution patterns may overlap.

CROWDSTRIKE’S ISRAELI CYBERSECURITY NETWORK
CrowdStrike has also become increasingly integrated with Israel’s cybersecurity industry.

By 2026, its Israeli acquisitions included:

• Preempt Security
• Bionic
• Flow Security
• Adaptive Shield
• Seraphic Security

These acquisitions mean that Israeli-developed technology, Israeli cybersecurity personnel and Israeli research-and-development teams contribute directly to CrowdStrike’s larger platform.

CrowdStrike therefore sits inside several overlapping systems:
• Minnesota government cybersecurity
• US federal intelligence and law enforcement
• Democratic Party political operations
• Russiagate attribution
• Ukrainian political controversy
• Israeli cybersecurity development
• US national-security policymaking

That makes CrowdStrike more than a passing detail in the Minnesota story.

WHAT DID CROWDSTRIKE ACTUALLY PROTECT?
There is currently no public confirmation that CrowdStrike was installed directly on the specific operational technology attacked at Minnesota’s water facilities.

CrowdStrike primarily protects conventional endpoints:
• Employee computers
• Windows and Linux servers
• Credentials and user accounts
• Enterprise networks
• Malware and ransomware entry points

The Minnesota attack reportedly involved operational technology, potentially including:
• Programmable logic controllers
• SCADA systems
• Human-machine interfaces
• Remote telemetry equipment
• Pump and pressure controls
• Vendor remote-access gateways

If attackers connected directly to exposed PLCs, they could potentially bypass CrowdStrike-protected municipal computers entirely.

That makes the contractor, network and equipment records critical.

THE ISRAELI CRITICAL-INFRASTRUCTURE CYBER ECOSYSTEM

There is another layer.

The COVID-19 Cyber Threat Intelligence League—CTI League—was established in March 2020 as an international volunteer cybersecurity organization.

One of its four founders was Ohad Zaidenberg, an Israeli cybersecurity researcher and former commander in Unit 8200—Israel’s military signals-intelligence and cyber unit.

CTI League offered pro-bono cybersecurity assistance to:

• Hospitals
• Pharmaceutical companies
• Law enforcement
• Federal agencies
• State and local governments
• Critical-infrastructure operators (Water, Nuclear, Grid)

It partnered with CISA and Health-ISAC while generally withholding the identities of facilities receiving assistance.

CTI League was not technically an Israeli company.
Nevertheless, its Unit 8200 connection and access to American critical infrastructure are directly relevant when mapping the relationships between intelligence, government and private cybersecurity organizations.

Several major operational-technology security companies also originated within Israel’s military-intelligence and cybersecurity ecosystem:

• Claroty was launched through Team8. Its early president, Nadav Zafrir, previously commanded Unit 8200.

• CyberX was founded by Omer Schneider and Nir Giller, both veterans of an elite Israeli cyber-intelligence unit.

Microsoft acquired CyberX and incorporated its technology into Microsoft Defender for IoT.

• Indegy was an Israeli industrial-cybersecurity company acquired by Tenable.

Its technology became part of Tenable OT Security.

• Waterfall Security Solutions is headquartered in Israel and specializes in water, energy, nuclear and other critical infrastructure.

• Armis, SCADAfence, Radiflow and OTORIO were also created within Israel’s cybersecurity ecosystem.

A substantial portion of the technology protecting Western industrial infrastructure was developed by personnel who previously worked inside Israel’s military-intelligence system.

That relationship deserves transparency—especially when cybersecurity attribution could be used to influence decisions involving war.

THE COMPANIES CONFIRMED WITHIN MINNESOTA

CrowdStrike:

MNIT’s Whole-of-State Managed Detection and Response provider, protecting more than 55,000 government endpoints across over 200 public entities.

Tenable Security Center:

Used by MNIT for vulnerability scanning, including limited scanning of IoT and industrial-control devices.

Tenable acquired Israeli operational-technology company Indegy.

Tenable co-founder Ron Gula previously worked at the NSA.

Former Tenable CEO Amit Yoran graduated from West Point, served as an Air Force officer and became the founding director of DHS’s National Cyber Security Division.

Check Point CloudGuard:

An Israeli cybersecurity platform used by Minnesota agencies for cloud and web-application protection.

Check Point founders Gil Shwed and Shlomo Kramer came from Israel’s Unit 8200 military-intelligence environment.

Microsoft:
Broadly used across Minnesota government.
Microsoft acquired Israeli operational-technology company CyberX and incorporated it into Defender for IoT.
Microsoft also operates at the center of US military cloud infrastructure, Ukrainian cyber defense and Israeli cybersecurity development.

Amazon Web Services:

Provides cloud infrastructure and related security services to Minnesota agencies.

AWS also operates classified infrastructure for the CIA and provides cloud services across the Department of Defense.

F5:
Used by Minnesota agencies for web-application firewall and cloud-security functions.

Akamai:
Used for web-application protection and DDoS-related services and connected to the Israeli cybersecurity industry through multiple acquisitions.
THE COMPLETE NETWORK
The complete network is therefore not simply:

Minnesota → CrowdStrike.

It is:

MINNESOTA PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE
↓

text:
On this day in 1777, the Continental Congress did something that sounds completely insane on paper. They commissioned a nineteen-year-old French aristocrat with zero combat experience as a major general in the American army. His name was the Marquis de Lafayette, and betting on him turned out to be one of the best decisions they ever made.

Understand how unlikely this was. Lafayette was a teenager, rich, titled, and green as grass, who had defied his own king and slipped out of France against orders to come fight for a revolution that was losing. Congress was drowning in foreign officers demanding rank and money, and they were sick of it. What set Lafayette apart was a single line in his offer: he would serve at his own expense and take no pay. He did not want money. He wanted the cause. That, plus a letter backed by Benjamin Franklin, flipped Congress from annoyed to charmed.

The gamble paid off almost immediately. Just weeks later at the Battle of Brandywine, this untested kid general was shot through the leg, and instead of going down he stayed up rallying retreating troops, helping turn a rout into an orderly withdrawal before he would let anyone treat the wound. Washington, who had lost his own son years earlier, more or less adopted him. The feeling was mutual.

And here is why July 31 matters. That teenager grew into one of the most important men of the entire Revolution. Four years later it was Lafayette, maneuvering across Virginia, who helped pin Cornwallis at Yorktown and set up the victory that won the war. The old commanders trusted a nineteen-year-old volunteer with a general's stars, and he spent the rest of the war proving they were right.

Some have praised the new category as a way to expand opportunities for Asian artists. Others, however, have questioned whether it simply places Asian artists into a separate box rather than allowing them to compete equally.
The Grammys, which have long faced criticism for being overly favorable toward the white mainstream music industry, may have brought this controversy upon themselves.

In other words, BTS's boycott represents a refreshing shift in perspective: refusing to be confined by a system created by others.
It will be interesting to see what changes this confident declaration of independence will bring.

text:
You’ll never believe what happened to me while working as a Scripter for a 250,000 member Roblox military roleplay group called UBA (Upsetioz British Army)

I worked 60 days straight, clocking 8-12 hours on systems that they micromanaged and wanted 10+ changes per task, ignored my suggestions to speed things up, and blamed me for the time it was taking to complete. 

They wanted quality > quantity but were upset that they had to pay for it

Starting for the first two weeks, things were good. I made $80/day, sometimes more with bonus if they needed the work done that day.

After 2 weeks I experienced the first red flag. All of my hard work and overtime + full commitment to their project ultimately lead to one thing I never expected.. a pay decrease 

Because I’m a reasonable person and willing to accept that my work is a bit slower than kids using AI agents, I ultimately let them talk me into working for $50/day for the same amount of effort and dedication to their group because I valued the consistency. (Big mistake)

After another 6 weeks I was in a really bad position because I had hoped to get a pay increase by then and wasn’t making enough to pay my bills + focusing too much time on their game for too little pay. 

They try to psychologically manipulate you into believing that your work is worth less so they can ask for lower prices, and I bet it works on the kids I saw which they target to work for them illegally for slave wages earned in Robux.

After notifying the owner that I would be taking some time off because I need a break to recover for a week, I was constantly asked if I can get started before the week ended. 

Upon saying I needed a break, I was forced to do a test session the next day. During the session, the owner started falsely claiming things were only half done and discrediting my work when he’s not a trained tester. Nothing he said helped fix anything. 

The truth is that it was over 90% complete but he has no technical expertise. I was ironing out the complex code that they wanted for who gets to see the script based on who can chat with others and that’s still something that’s new to the platform.

I found out the bad news that I was replaced because I didn’t come back from my break early. 

I have to pay my bills so I offered to help them setup QA department since it was a big factor in me not being able to get things tested properly. 

After a month of saying they were going to have me get started on that, I told them the price would be raising if they don’t lock in soon- not even in a disrespectful way. Just wanted to make sure they were serious.

Instead of locking in as I hoped they would, I get told I’m getting “permanently off-boarded” and that they will not be hiring me again for any reason and blocked

I found an old group messsge we had so I sent them a message apologizing for the confusion and said they can make the payment if they want to still. They ultimately dedicated to send it then, but it never would have if I wasn’t the bigger person and applogize after I did nothing wrong. 

They paid 30k robux and made it very clear that they did not want to pay me to maintain it or manage it and they wanted me to do it for free. 

I said I could do it for $35 a week and they refused and said they’d pay $35 one more time in a few days but I’d already been working unpaid for days.

I did everything I could to step up, trying to prove that I can help grow and manage their team- but I was always held back by 2 micro-managers in charge of the group who had no technical expertise.  

They didn’t believe it was possible to put 12 hour days in based on my output (I’m not an AI) but I was able to do those hours because that’s how motivated I was to have a long term opportunity and “career.” 

I found out the hard way that would not be the case. 

Today I officially cut ties. After paying for 6+ weeks all of a sudden they “don’t have the money anymore” and are a “small studio”

text:
Two Killed, Two Wounded in Early Morning Shooting at Chicago Gas Station

Chicago, Illinois — On July 2, 2026, at approximately  a.m., four people were shot outside a BP gas station in the 7600 block of South Halsted Street in the Auburn Gresham neighborhood.

According to the Chicago Police Department, four unknown male offenders approached a group standing outside the station and opened fire. The offenders, described as wearing all dark clothing with one in red and white shoes, then fled on foot through a nearby alley. Surveillance video later released by police shows the group approaching the location. Some reports noted the use of handguns and rifles.

Surbezz Clark, 53, of Chicago, and Carlos A. Jones, 46, of Chicago, were pronounced dead at the University of Chicago Medical Center. The Cook County medical examiner’s office confirmed the deaths. A 35-year-old woman and a 33-year-old man were also struck and transported to the same hospital in critical condition.

The Chicago Police Department’s Area Two detectives are investigating under case number JK316902. No arrests have been made. Police released surveillance footage on or about July 29, 2026, seeking public assistance in identifying the offenders. Cook County Crime Stoppers offered a reward of up to $10,000 for information leading to an arrest. Tips may be submitted anonymously via https://t.co/dEsPyDrtaD or by contacting Area Two detectives at (312) 747-8271.

Public arrest records list prior incidents involving Surbezz Clark. These include a June 7, 2014, arrest in Chicago for aggravated assault with use of a deadly weapon and issuance of a warrant; a September 25, 2014, arrest for issuance of a warrant; a September 20, 2017, arrest for issuance of a warrant; and a September 1, 2018, arrest for possession of a controlled substance (other amount narcotic Schedule I and II).

Sources: Chicago Police Department community alert and video release

text:
🚨 NFL CAMP BUZZ  - July 31  RAPID FIRE 🚨
 
🌵 Arizona Cardinals

- RB room / Jeremiyah Love / Tyler Allgeier
Mike LaFleur said he wants to split up the RB room: “Not one RB can take all 65 snaps.” The Cardinals may take a Year 1 Bijan/Allgeier-style approach, with Love handling the bulk but not being overloaded. Current camp carry split noted: Allgeier 21, Love 18. Allgeier has taken the first 11-on-11 snaps with the first team before Love rotates in.

- Jeremiyah Love development
LaFleur is not worried about what Love looks like on Sept. 13. Love said the biggest challenge has been the mental aspect, he is leaning on James Conner for advice, wants preseason reps, likes how Arizona is using him in the passing game, and says he needs to improve reading coverages.

- Michael Wilson / Marvin Harrison Jr.
Marvin Harrison Jr. has more camp targets than Michael Wilson so far, 17 to 12. Harrison is usually the lone WR on the field in 3TE sets. LaFleur wants to use Wilson creatively, including jet motion handoffs and even lining him up at TE in heavy formations to create defensive confusion.

🍑 Atlanta Falcons

- QB room / Tua Tagovailoa / Michael Penix Jr.
Tua returned in a limited fashion with a tight back, doing individual drills and a half-speed walkthrough but no full-speed team reps. He said the limitation is mostly precautionary and that this back issue is new. Michael Penix Jr. returned after a scheduled rest day and did individual drills plus one 7-on-7 session. Jack Strand and Cooper Rush took the full team work, with Strand getting most 11-on-11 reps.

- Bijan Robinson
Bijan’s hold-in continued. He was present and even did pushups after a drill, but did not practice. Tua said, “We’re waiting for Bijan to get paid.”

- Zachariah Branch
Kevin Stefanski praised Branch’s makeup. Branch has been really impressive early — effortless explosiveness/speed, leaving defenders behind. Tua said Branch is “usually open.” Only noted mistake was a route miscommunication.

- Cooper Rush / Jack Strand
Rush had a nice team period with three straight completions and seems to be warming up to the system. Strand continues drawing praise and has improved his roster chances.

🐦‍⬛ Baltimore Ravens

- Lamar Jackson / offense usage
Lamar is expected to be under center more with play action and bootlegs. This could b a bounce-back signal because it should help him rhythm-wise and open bootleg/run-game looks.

- Young WRs over veteran signing
The Ravens appear more likely to count on Devontez Walker, Elijah Sarratt and Ja’Kobi Lane rather than sign a meaningful veteran. The rookies are expected to get opportunities to develop.

- Tez Walker / Matt Hibner
Practice 3: Tez Walker made a nice end-zone grab, bobbling initially before securing it. Matt Hibner was used a bunch in the receiving game and is “stacking some good days.”

🦬 Buffalo Bills

- Skyler Bell / Keon Coleman WR3 battle
Skyler Bell is in line for WR3 duties and competing with Keon Coleman. The Bills appear intentional about getting Bell reps with Josh Allen; every route/catch drill pass to Bell came from Allen on this day.

- RB passing-game usage
Bills RBs are being used more in the passing game, including play-action looks where the RB leaks out for routes. This is Pete Carmichael’s influence and the key is whether this materially impacts James Cook.

🐻 Chicago Bears

- Colston Loveland / Rome Odunze / Caleb Williams
Big day for Loveland and Odunze. Caleb connected with Loveland repeatedly in an 11-on-11 two-minute ramp-up: 6-yard drag, 6-yard hitch, 10-yard hitch. Odunze had back-to-back deep receptions, including a bobbled one-handed catch.

- Luther Burden / role watch
Keep watching how the Bears describe roles between Rome, Loveland and Burden. Short-route players are framed as bigger boom/lower bust pieces.

- Kyle Monangai / Salvon Ahmed
Monangai missed a second straight practice. Salvon Ahmed took Monangai’s reps behind D’Andre Swift.

🟤 Cleveland Browns

- Shedeur Sanders / QB rotation
Prime was seen coaching up Shedeur after Day 2 of Browns camp. Shedeur was QB1 today and got first-team reps. Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion and Isaiah Bond all appeared to get targets from him.

- Browns WR reps
Majority of first-team WR reps went to Isaiah Bond, Jerry Jeudy and KC Concepcion. Monken’s “earn it” approach was noted.

⭐ Dallas Cowboys

- CeeDee Lamb
CeeDee was on the field getting early work at 7:45 a.m., reinforcing WR1 preparation.

- Jaydon Blue
Blue is off to a strong start and alternated with Javonte Williams with the first team. He is being discussed as a complement to Javonte, especially as a pass catcher and space player. Current read: possible 5-10 touch complementary role, with more upside if Javonte misses time, but not necessarily a full 15+ touch role.

🐴 Denver Broncos

- Jaylen Waddle / Evan Engram / Bo Nix / Marvin Mims
Waddle had a really good first day of camp. Evan Engram was arguably the star, catching a pass from every QB, including a 50+ yard bomb from Jarrett Stidham. Play of the day was Bo Nix hitting Marvin Mims deep for 50 yards.

🦁 Detroit Lions

- Isiah Pacheco / Sione Vaki
Sione Vaki is splitting first-team reps with Isiah Pacheco. 

🦅 Philadelphia Eagles

- Tank Bigsby / Saquon Barkley
Tank Bigsby and Saquon Barkley are reportedly splitting first-team reps 50-50. Don't overreact yet because it could be Saquon load management, but Eagles insiders seem to think there may be something real to Tank’s role. 

🧀 Green Bay Packers

- Tucker Kraft
Kraft is coming off PUP and practicing. He said the doctor told him his knee looks “spectacular,” almost like the doctor had never seen a knee rehab like his.

- MarShawn Lloyd
Speculative but positive note: Lloyd is viewed by the writer as more than a third-down back — potentially a feature back in the making — and has been catching passes out of the backfield.

- Packers offensive tempo / WR route shares
Matt LaFleur emphasized better tempo and getting in/out of the huddle quicker. The note links that to fewer substitutions and potentially higher route shares for Packers WRs.

- Matthew Golden
Golden made multiple standout catches: an absurd over-the-shoulder deep catch from Jordan Love up the right sideline, and another leaping catch between Xavier McKinney and Zaire Franklin for 18 yards. Best catch of camp so far.

🐂 Houston Texans

- Jayden Higgins
DeMeco Ryans praised Higgins’ Year 2 jump. Houston is moving him around more, including inside/slot looks. Ryans said Higgins is making plays wherever they put him and that they need someone opposite Nico Collins to step up; Higgins “can be that guy.” Higgins also made tough catches against Derek Stingley with C.J. Stroud showing confidence to layer throws in.

🐎 Indianapolis Colts

- DJ Giddens / RB2 battle
Colts RB2 alert: DJ Giddens is currently ahead. This matters because he had been splitting with Seth McGowan when Jonathan Taylor missed OTAs. A veteran signing is also still possible.

- Deebo Samuel fallout / WR need
Deebo reportedly had an option with the Colts before returning to San Francisco. Ricky Pearsall’s uncertain status could make it likely the Colts sign a WR, with Keenan Allen speculated as a fit.

🐆 Jacksonville Jaguars

- Trevor Lawrence
Lawrence was fantastic on Day 3, especially in the red zone. He threw TDs to Jakobi Meyers, Bhayshul Tuten, Brian Thomas Jr. twice and Parker Washington.

- Bhayshul Tuten
Tuten continues stacking strong practices while Chris Rodriguez is not doing team drills. He showed explosiveness and pass-catching ability with two long runs and a receiving TD. With Rodriguez out, Tuten looks like a bellcow-type option in the current practice setup.

- Chris Rodriguez
Rodriguez remains out/not doing team drills, creating the window for Tuten.

- Parker Washington
Washington keeps showing up. Another strong practice, and he was the first player seen at the Jaguars facility at 5:20 a.m., already stretching before his workout. This is on-brand for a player trying to secure an extension.

- Travis Hunter
Hunter’s 11-on-11 snap tracker: Day 1: 8 defensive, 4 offensive. Day 2: 8 defensive, 4 offensive. Day 3: 8 defensive, 7 offensive. Everything is scripted, but his offensive usage moved closer to 50/50. He is working outside and running downfield routes, not gadget reps, though sample size remains small.

🏹 Kansas City Chiefs

- Kenneth Walker
Dan Graziano says it sounds like the Chiefs intend to use Walker as a full-on workhorse. The listed pecking order was: Kenneth Walker, Brashard Smith, Emari Demercado, Emmett Johnson. Walker was also involved in the screen game, including a quick screen from Mahomes that could have gone for a long TD.

- Patrick Mahomes / Cyrus Allen
Andy Reid said Cyrus Allen has done a nice job, QBs trust him, and he had a productive two days, though he needs to clean some things up. With Rashee Rice not working team drills, Allen has been Mahomes’ favorite target early. There was also a teaching moment where Allen lined up on the wrong side and Mahomes redirected him.

- Rashee Rice medical note
Jeff Mueller noted Rice’s legs look sluggish/heavy and that he is clearly not moving at 100% while rehabbing from a knee scope procedure.

- Mahomes rushing note
Expect less designed/overall rushing volume for Mahomes, but still expect instinctive scrambles. The writer is not fading him coming off ACL/LCL.

⚡ Los Angeles Chargers

- Brennen Thompson / WR battle
Brennen Thompson had a good practice on Justin Herbert throws and is battling Tre Harris for snaps. Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey are described as the top two WRs.

- Justin Herbert / Mike McDaniel scheme
OC Mike McDaniel praised Herbert’s progress with footwork and new scheme responsibilities. Herbert has impressed with comfort in what the staff introduced in spring.

🐏 Los Angeles Rams

- Sean McDermott visit
Former Bills head coach Sean McDermott visited the Rams to observe how they operate during his time away.

☠️ Las Vegas Raiders

- Ashton Jeanty
Jeanty said in a YouTube video that whoever is in his way, “it’s bad for you,” and that he is here to show what he brings. There's a possibility of Jeanty seeing more pass-game usage and even being second on the team in targets.

- Brock Bowers / Michael Mayer
Bowers and Mayer have made plays in heavy personnel packages. The staff is excited about Mayer’s versatility and incorporating him.

- Raiders WR3 battle
Jack Bech and Dont’e Thornton are both getting first-team reps, with Bech doing better so far. They are battling for WR3. This may not be highly valuable if the Raiders lean into 12 personnel, but it matters because the WR room lacks a clear stud.

- Raiders Day 3
Brock Bowers had his way all day. Jalen Nailor got more involved and caught a TD from Fernando Mendoza. Kirk Cousins and Bowers connected on two TDs. Mendoza threw a back-shoulder TD to Malik Benson. Cousins threw an INT.

🟣 Minnesota Vikings

- Kyler Murray / J.J. McCarthy
Kyler took a hefty amount of snaps with the starters, while J.J. McCarthy spent more time with the 2s.

🇺🇸 New England Patriots

- Kayshon Boutte
Boutte spoke unprompted about potentially being somewhere else, while still saying he is taking things day by day. Mike Giardi says Boutte is still available for trade. Boutte knows his Patriots days could be numbered.

- Drake Maye / A.J. Brown
Maye said he and A.J. Brown have gone through some of Brown’s old film to review route details and how Brown likes to run them.

- Patriots camp notes
Maye is stacking good padded practices and was efficient/accurate, especially in the red zone. Productive days for A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas and Eli Raridon. Hunter Henry had a great bobbled TD catch.

⚜️ New Orleans Saints

- Chris Olave
Olave said he leaned heavily on Michael Thomas during extension negotiations, calling him nearly every day for advice.

- Tyler Shough / Saints vibes
Adam Schefter said there are great vibes around the Saints, that Shough looked like he belonged last year, and that they could be dangerous this season.

🗽 New York Giants

- Malik Nabers
Peter Schrager said Nabers has the opportunity to be a top-five WR or better over his career and expects him to be the focal point of the Giants offense.

🐾 Carolina Panthers

- Chris Brazzell II
Brazzell has been placed on IR.

- Jonathon Brooks
Brooks hype has been strong. Mike Kaye said Brooks has looked sharp, is cutting well, showing impressive hands and gaining rhythm, but that it is still Chuba Hubbard’s backfield for now.

🟡 Pittsburgh Steelers

- Roman Wilson / Germie Bernard
Mike McCarthy said the Wilson/Bernard battle is “competition for opportunity.” Both showed in spring that they can play all three WR spots. 

- Kaleb Johnson Kaleb Johnson has gotten some plays with the 1s, but that has been true throughout camp. He is currently the No. 3 RB.

🌉 San Francisco 49ers

- Deebo Samuel
Deebo likely slides back into the Z receiver role he had from 2019-2024. The medical note says Deebo was not as cooked last year as perceived and could be a flex option for contenders.

- De’Zhaun Stribling
Mike Evans singled out Stribling as a young WR standing out. Stribling keeps flashing, likely can play big slot, and could find the field even with Deebo back.

🌊 Seattle Seahawks

- Tory Horton
Horton said he had surgery for a fractured tibia in February. He discovered a crack in his shin after Week 9 and eventually had surgery. He now has two rods in the leg and says he feels good. 

🏴‍☠️ Tampa Bay Buccaneers

- Baker Mayfield contract drama
Adam Schefter said the Bucs were offering Mayfield over $50M per year and felt their offers were competitive. The Bucs are reportedly unhappy with how Mayfield spoke about the organization. NFL Network note says Tampa made multiple two-year extension runs over $50M/year, while Baker wanted more security and respect.

- Bucky Irving / Kenny Gainwell
Bucky was given the most carries Friday while Gainwell was used primarily as a receiver out of the backfield. Irving had the biggest run of the day from a pony package on a delayed handoff and looked good.

- Emeka Egbuka
Egbuka looks like the top WR so far at camp. He is working primarily as the Z, but Zac Robinson is moving him all over the formation.

⚔️ Tennessee Titans

- Wan’Dale Robinson
Robinson runs a lot of option routes that are specific to him in this offense. He is tasked with taking pressure off the offensive line and is expected to lead the team in receptions.

🪖 Washington Commanders

- WR room / Treylon Burks
Treylon Burks sat with foot soreness. He is the presumed outside WR2 when healthy. Current starting WRs are Terry McLaurin, Luke McCaffrey and likely Burks. Expectation is a committee approach and lots of 12 personnel.

- Chig Okonkwo
If Washington does not add Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo is speculatively mentioned as a possible second option in the pass game.

- Stefon Diggs monitoring
Washington is monitoring the Diggs situation. John Keim reportedly believes Diggs is the only WR addition that makes sense for the team.

text:
I've debated a lot of people, but Dinesh was different in one respect. He's the only person I've debated for whom the more he talked, the better it was for me. He highlighted the errors of Dispensationalism better than I ever could. And there's one example that stands out to me. 

To argue that Abraham did NOT believe in Jesus, and was NOT justified by faith in Jesus (a tragic and heretical position to begin with), he argued that the Bible doesn’t REALLY mean that Abraham believed in Jesus, because of use of the word “imputed” in Galatians 3:6 (which means "to lay to ones' account) means that Abraham believed in God the Father, and then faith in Jesus was imputed to Him, as though he did believe in Jesus, when in fact, he didn't. 

Those of you who know how imputation works are already having seizures, but hang in there. It gets worse.

For clarity, the verse reads, “For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness." 

This is where Christians get the idea of “imputation by faith.” The way the gospel works is that our sins were imputed to Jesus (“He who had no sins became sin on our behalf” - 2 Cor 5:21) - the same way that sins of the Israelites were metaphorically imputed to bulls and goats on the Day of Atonement in Leviticus 16:21-22 - then, with Jesus being killed on our behalf, and absorbing for us the wrath of God, Jesus’ righteousness is then imputed to our account. It’s “the great exchange,” as I’ve always called it. He took our sin and punishment. We take His righteousness. 

Got it? Good.

Dinesh was using the word “imputation” correctly - “laying to one’s account” - but he was saying that Abraham’s faith in God the Father had imputed to Him faith in God the Son. But that’s NOT what is being imputed there. What’s being imputed is NOT faith. What’s being imputed is RIGHTEOUSNESS. The righteousness of Jesus was imputed to Abraham by Abraham’s faith in Jesus. Faith is NEVER imputed. Righteousness is imputed. Re-read the verse. Familiarize with the concept. Go read some theology books on soteriology. Whatever you have to do.

People, listen to me. Dispensationalism is a bad idea that requires the constant butchering of essential Biblical doctrines to make it fit into Scripture. This is but one example of the tragic consequences of a single bad idea when injected into Scripture, and before you know it, the gospel itself is being butchered like a bullock fresh off the peace offering pile. 

Dinesh D’Souza is taken as a serious man with deeply held Christian beliefs and thinks that Abraham was justified without faith in the Messiah, and that imputation imputes faith, instead of righteousness. This is an error with severe soteriological implications that a well-catechized ten-year-old should know better than.

Dispensationalism retards (aka hinders, delays, obstructs) basic biblical knowledge and doctrinal growth. On paper, Dinesh is allegedly one of the best that Dispensationalism has to offer. And he came up with an imputation theory so bizarre it deserves its own heresy term. 

And if Dispensationalists wanted to be honest and develop some legit street cred as impartial and serious about Biblical doctrine, they should be standing in line to condemn Dinesh's interpretation of what imputation is and the danger that presents to the gospel. If faith can be imputed, then that is the death knell of the Exclusivity of Christ.

text:
Lughnasadh marks the first harvest, traditionally celebrated on August 1st. 

In ancient times, this was not a quiet, passive day. It was a massive assembly called an Aonach, instituted by Lugh to honor the immense physical labor of his foster mother, Tailtiu, who died of exhaustion clearing the forests of Ireland for agriculture. 

Our ancestors honored her through sweat, skill, and discipline. They held fierce athletic games, contests of strength, and showcases of master craftsmanship. The festival was deeply tied to human effort, physical conditioning, and transforming raw nature. They put real skin in the game. 

Today, many try to honor these days with surface-level gestures or store-bought items that cost no actual effort. Placing a mass-produced item on an altar is a shallow copy of a worldview built on hard work and survival. 

We do not need to sacrifice bulls or hold chariot races, but the core drive remains the same: offering your own time, energy, and labor. 

Testing your physical endurance or working a raw material with your hands is the truest translation of Lughnasadh for modern life. It can be as simple as taking a rough piece of raw Carnelian stone, spending hours hand-shaping it with a diamond file while meditating, and leaving that finished work under a wild White Oak. The object matters far less than the personal energy you invested to shape it. 

When the old world fell, the first spiritual cycle ended. Much was lost so that we could learn how to actively rebuild the connection ourselves. 

We are in a renewed cycle now. You are never closer to the gods than when you are actively thinking, creating, and exerting real discipline to build that connection. 

Understand why our ancestors offered what they did. Find what represents true effort and mastery in your life today, and offer that instead. 

Restore the bridge. Make the effort real. That is how you honor Lugh on Lughnasadh (Loo-nah-sah).

$GDX 

$GDX gapped lower today before and is printing a spinning top candle, highlighting continued indecision as price trades lower within a falling wedge. 

Momentum remains weak, with both the RSI and MACD in bearish territory, while price continues to trade below key moving averages. 

Although a falling wedge can eventually lead to a bullish reversal, that signal has not materialized yet.

News Flashback

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
ROBOTAXI

NEW TODAY
- Testers (tslaming): GOOD NEWS 📰 Eric Early, Tesla’s Robotaxi and Cybercab engineering lead, just teased that massive upgrades are coming to the Robotaxi fleet “soon” 🔥 Since he kept the exact details…
- Folder totals: Robotaxi 121 (+1) + Fleet 4 (0 new) → 125 unique

WHAT IT IS
- Tesla’s paid autonomous ride service. You book a car in the Robotaxi app. The car drives. There is no human driver on unsupervised rides.
- Live cars today are mostly Model Y. The purpose-built Cybercab is the volume vehicle testers say Tesla is prioritizing.
- Camera-only vision. Tesla VP of AI Ashok Elluswamy: no lidar, radar, or HD maps required for safe operation on this stack.
- This how-to merges the public Robotaxi service folder with Owning Robotaxi Fleet (owner / private-fleet economics). Not Cybercab-only bookmarks.

HOW IT WORKS
- Download the Tesla Robotaxi app and join the waitlist. Official robotaxi (Sep 2025): app is available to all; access expands over time.
- Book the ride in Tesla’s app. Elon: Tesla will not partner with Uber or Lyft. “We will have enough demand.”
- Unsupervised means no safety driver. Supervised cities still have a person in the car.
- Official robotaxi (Aug 27): service hours are 6am to 10pm, 7 days/week. Unsupervised fleet is a lot bigger. Upgraded vehicle distribution and routing so you wait less.
- Testers: you can change destination and keep the same trip for multiple stops.
- Cars return to a depot or homebase and park themselves (Houston footage).
- Ashok: FSD v15 is already running on Model Y robotaxis and will run on Cybercab.
- Testers: Tesla is limiting Model Y conversions to prioritize Cybercab, built with an unboxed modular process.
- Testers (Aug 24): Tesla expects Cybercab to replace Model Ys in the Robotaxi fleet over time and become the highest-volume vehicle there. Testers flag Sept 3 / 9/3 as the Cybercab strategy moment. Austin public Cybercab rides described as “imminent.”

HOW TO USE
- Official robotaxi: download the app, join the waitlist.
- Official robotaxi (Aug 27): rides run 6am to 10pm every day. Unsupervised fleet is a lot bigger; routing upgrade is meant to cut wait time.
- Testers: booking is in the app. One Orlando rider paid with an X Money card.
- Tesla site (as quoted): app in 29 languages; service animals; space for some wheelchairs and assistive devices.
- Testers: vehicles in Nevada must be marked “Robotaxi.”
- After the Aug 20 Nevada approval, testers say Tesla still has to finish vehicle inspections, insurance, and published rates before paid rides start there.

OWNING / FLEET (from Owning Robotaxi Fleet dump)
- Elon (Feb 2026, also in Robotaxi folder): Tesla owners will be able to add their cars to the Robotaxi network; Tesla collects 25% of revenue.
- Fleet testers frame the network like Airbnb for cars: owner adds vehicle; Tesla handles software, routing, payments, rider experience; platform fee often modeled ~25–35%; owner keeps the rest after operating costs (tester).
- Fleet / Teslaconomics (Mar 2026): ~$30k/yr net profit per Robotaxi to owner is a base-case assumption from analyst models + Tesla long-term vision — after platform fee, charging, tires, maintenance, insurance, cleaning. No official real-world owner earnings in this dump. Profit/mile chatter ~$0.25–$0.50 after costs at 50k–100k+ miles/yr in high-demand areas.
- Fleet / Teslaconomics: Cybercab cost chatter ~$25k–$30k; Elon told that tester production was starting in ~1 month (Mar 2026 context — treat as dated tester claim). Rough capital for a ~$1M/yr fleet ~$850k–$1M in vehicles (tester arithmetic).
- Fleet / chamath: intends to buy and deploy large fleets nationally when possible; expects payback and positive FCF in under 2 years (tester / investor claim, not Official Tesla).
- Fleet / BrianRoemmele: “all in” on buying into the owning-fleet thesis now; separate Optimus ownership program mentioned but not published in this dump.
- Fleet / tslaming (Mar 2026): then only 8 unsupervised Austin robotaxis — historical; do not use as current fleet size (Robotaxi dump Aug 23 tester: 908 total).
- Testers / Teslaconomics (Aug 25, Robotaxi folder): “owning your own Tesla Robotaxi fleet can one day make you financially free.” Still a tester slogan — no Official owner-earnings number in this dump.
- CONFLICT / caution: owner earnings, Cybercab sticker, ROI, and payback are tester models. Dump explicitly says none of it is guaranteed. Do not treat as Official Tesla guidance.

SERVICE AREA / CITIES
- Unsupervised (no safety driver), as listed May 2026: Austin, TX (launched Jun 22, 2025); Dallas, TX and Houston, TX (launched Apr 18, 2026).
- Supervised (safety driver), as listed May 2026: SF Bay Area, CA (launched Apr 18, 2026).
- Testers: Bay Area rides to and from SFO. Earlier: San Jose Airport pickup.
- Testers: an Orlando rider reviewed a live Robotaxi trip (Jul 2026). Aug 21 testers also list Orlando and Tampa as live; that is not on the May 2026 official city list.
- Testers (Aug 25 Teslaconomics): 7 metro areas live. Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa ramping unsupervised; Bay Area still safety-driver. Treat as tester city list, not Official May 2026 list.
- Testers (Aug 27 travel_invest): recap of Official hours post lists 6 target cities — Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa. Tester translation, not a new Official city list.
- Nevada (Aug 20, 2026): full network permit for paid public service. Start small in Clark County / Las Vegas; Tesla can expand elsewhere in the state after notifying the commission.
- Testers (Aug 23): Nevada approved Tesla for up to 5,000 autonomous vehicles, up from a 10-car interim limit. Tesla said it would be “extremely happy” to have around 2,500 running within a year.
- Testers (May 2026) said Tesla was also aiming at Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa.
- Hiring and test-vehicle posts (treat as signals, not live service): Arizona, Florida, Washington, New York, Pennsylvania, Massachusetts, California, D.C., plus a Germany Arzfeld pilot with a safety driver and Japan Kanagawa job listings.
- Ashok: expanding to a new city is getting cheaper; the end state is operating whole states, not city by city.

ACCESS AND PLANS
- Official: Robotaxi app waitlist. Access expands as cities open.
- Testers (Aug 27 WorldlyReviewer): received an email from Tesla advertising Robotaxi. Tester report of Tesla marketing, not a new Official service announcement.
- Elon (Feb 2026): Tesla owners will be able to add their cars to the Robotaxi network; Tesla collects 25% of revenue.
- Testers (JPMorgan via folder posts): robotaxi operating cost about $0.50–$0.60 per mile vs $2.50–$3.00 for typical ride-hail; long-term platform goal $0.30 per mile. Older Morgan Stanley note used $0.81 per mile vs Waymo $1.36–$1.43.
- Folder testers argue Tesla scales on existing Model Y / Cybercab manufacturing and Superchargers, vs lidar-heavy custom cars.
- Testers (Aug 23): Waymo’s latest self-driving hardware reportedly costs around $20K.
- See OWNING / FLEET for private-owner economics from the Owning Robotaxi Fleet folder.

SAFETY
- Elon: scale as fast as possible, but do not harm anyone. One injury becomes a worldwide headline and a regulatory clampdown.
- Ashok (Jul 2026): zero notable incidents over 380,000 unsupervised miles, across six cities in two states. Cameras only.
- Testers on NHTSA ADS data (Jun 16, 2025–Jul 15, 2026): zero collisions initiated by the Model Y ADS. Two new incidents were other drivers hitting a stopped or parked Robotaxi (Austin red-arrow stop; Dallas parked). No passengers, no injuries, no tow.
- Austin: testers said 100% of tracked robotaxi rides in that NHTSA window were unsupervised.
- Testers: 7x safer than the average human driver is an FSD claim in this folder, not a Robotaxi-only official stat.

FLEET AND INFRASTRUCTURE
- Official robotaxi (Aug 27): unsupervised fleet is a lot bigger; upgraded intelligence in vehicle distribution and routing. Testers (tslaming) say that gain is backend ops (demand forecasting, fleet placement), not a self-driving software change.
- Testers (Aug 23): 908 robotaxis in the total fleet. Treat as the latest tester count, not official.
- Testers (Aug 19): about 97 Cybercabs at the Houston Robotaxi lot. Model Ys and Cybercabs still rotating in the geofence.
- Testers: Tesla plans 80 wireless chargers in Austin as Phase 2 of a Robotaxi charging hub.
- Testers: private (not public) V4 Supercharger depots, including 56 stalls in Chandler / Phoenix East Valley; a Dallas-area fleet depot; a Las Vegas Cybercab wash/service site.
- Testers: scale needs charging, cleaning, and maintenance automated, not only FSD.
- Fleet-size tweets in this folder are days-to-months apart and disagree. Do not treat an old 500–600 car count (or the Mar 2026 “8 unsupervised in Austin” fleet-folder snapshot) as current.

USEFUL WORKFLOWS
- New city: download the Robotaxi app, join the waitlist, ride when your city opens.
- Live city: book in the Tesla app. Try a multi-stop trip if the app offers it.
- Airport: testers already used SFO and SJC where those pickups were live.
- Watch Nevada: paid Las Vegas service after the Aug 20 permit plus leftover admin steps; testers now cite a 5,000-vehicle cap.
- Watch Austin: testers say public Cybercab rides are “imminent.”
- Owning a fleet: not open as a turnkey product in this dump. Watch Elon’s owner-network comments + Tesla fee structure; treat $30k/yr and <2yr payback as tester models only.

KEY LINKS
- Robotaxi folder: https://t.co/H4gqqNAU8l
- Owning Robotaxi Fleet folder: https://t.co/dOlqygr8vA
- Official app waitlist: https://t.co/1cA1CkRGDe
- Official hours / bigger unsupervised fleet (Aug 27): https://t.co/dZaS0xi5Q2
- Nevada full permit (Aug 20): https://t.co/E2MiqQvHAV
- Dallas and Houston unsupervised launch: https://t.co/8UTZ9h9p6K
- Fleet economics tester thread: https://t.co/J7hTeygpFM
- Chamath fleet intent: https://t.co/DkAmO2Woey
- Testers Aug 25 Waymo/Tesla scale compare: https://t.co/zCNCpxP7eG
- Testers Aug 25 owning-fleet slogan: https://t.co/wv58yt9UAa
- Testers Aug 27 Tesla Robotaxi email ad: https://t.co/jmrdVJTp6W
